# Jira issue template

Use this template when drafting or creating a Stage 1 Jira work item. Fill in
every section; the Issue Analyst checks each one against the Definition of
Ready.

## Summary

<!-- One sentence describing the user-visible or infrastructure outcome. -->

## Scope

<!-- The bounded vertical slice this issue delivers. List concrete,
independently reviewable work items. -->

## Non-goals

<!-- Explicitly excluded work, including any deferred Stage 1 feature this
issue must not introduce (groups, attachments, reactions, edit/delete, read
receipts, typing indicators, presence, search, push notifications, calls,
blocking, moderation, end-to-end encryption, offline/PWA, production
deployment) and any adjacent product behavior owned by another story. -->

## Acceptance criteria

<!-- Numbered, independently testable statements. Each must be verifiable by
an automated check or explicit manual verification step. -->

1.

## Design links

<!-- Approved Figma frame links with an explicit user-approval reference, or
"Not applicable — no UI behavior." A Figma link alone is not approval
evidence. -->

## Dependencies and blockers

<!-- Parent epic, prerequisite issues, required merged PRs, and any
environment or tooling prerequisite. -->

## Test expectations

<!-- Required automated evidence: unit/component tests, API integration
tests, browser/accessibility tests, migration validation, and any other
scenario from the Stage 1 test plan this issue touches. -->

## Security considerations

<!-- Authentication, session, authorization, and cross-user data-isolation
impact. State "None" only if genuinely not applicable. -->

## Rollback

<!-- How the merged change can be safely reverted, including any migration
rollback step. -->

## One-PR feasibility

<!-- Confirm this scope is deliverable as one pull request, or state the
stop condition requiring scope review. -->
